ust.method: Overnight = New York closes strictly before each Jakarta close (New York shuts at about 04:00–05:00 Jakarta). Hedged = INDOGB 10Y minus β × US 10Y, β the trailing 26-week weekly beta known at the time. All variants walk-forward, z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks, thresholds ±0.5, hit rates over the next 4 weeks. The 'Beta 3Y' slot carries the INDOGB 15Y.

notes.headline: Still selling together: JCI −19% in four weeks, rupiah near record lows and the 10Y INDOGB +49bp to a new high of 7.72%, almost all of it local. Signal −0.87: bond sell-off
notes.now: Foreign money is still leaving Indonesia through stocks and the currency, and bonds keep paying for it. The JCI closed at 4,920 on Wednesday, 19% down in four weeks, after a politically driven early fall was reversed by a Rp265bn foreign net buy, the first in several sessions; USD/IDR is 2.0% weaker over four weeks at 18,155, a new high for the move. The 10Y INDOGB is up 49bp over the same span to 7.72%, the top of its five-year range, even though officials say non-residents still bought SBN in the third quarter. Three of the four signal parts point to a sell-off (JCI 4-week z −2.02, rupiah z +0.99, 10Y trend z +1.72), and only the spread part is bond-bullish: INDOGBs pay 277bp over Treasuries, 36bp more than their 26-week average (z +1.26), the 96th percentile of the past year. Treasuries explain almost none of it: the US 10Y fell 27bp in four weeks and the weekly beta is −0.10, so the 4-week move splits into +3bp 'global' and +46bp local. On the day the link held: Tuesday's 4bp New York sell-off implied about +1.2bp for INDOGBs at the 1-year daily beta of 0.29 against a +0.6bp actual move, and Wednesday's midterm rally in Asia (US 10Y about −5bp) is worth roughly −1.5bp, though the next-day beta is only 0.07; when the US 10Y moves 10bp or more, INDOGBs follow in the same direction 68–80% of the time. The signal has read sell-off since Oct 2 and the 10Y is 57bp higher since, a clear hit for this episode. Its full record is modest (Sharpe 0.37 since June 2022, sell-off calls right 54%), but since September 2024, when foreign flows took over, it scores 1.13 outright and 1.40 hedged. Our read for the next 2–4 weeks: stay underweight duration until BI acts and the rupiah holds; the spread cushion is the widest of the year, so the turn, when it comes, should be fast, and the first sign will be the JCI holding its lows with foreign buying for a week while USD/IDR stops rising.
notes.flip: The signal returns to neutral above −0.5: roughly, the JCI 4-week return back above −5% or the 10Y's 4-week rise slowing below 20bp, with USD/IDR flat or lower. A move to bond rally (above +0.5) needs a JCI rebound and a firmer rupiah together, the pattern that started the April 2025 rally. The policy triggers are a BI-Rate hike that steadies the rupiah (bearish for the front end on the day, bullish for the trend after) or MSCI softening its Standalone proposal.
phases: JCI 6,500–7,250 while the 10Y rose from 6.2% to a 7.58% peak in October 2022 as global rates surged; stocks held up on the commodity boom.
JCI 6,630–7,380 and 10Y 6.19–7.21%. Stocks and bonds drifted without a clear link, and the signal's calls lost money (Sharpe −0.3 from 2022 to August 2024).
JCI fell from 7,812 to 6,258 while the 10Y rose from 6.43% to 7.19%: stocks, rupiah and bonds sold off together, the pattern the signal is built for. Its record improves sharply from here.
JCI climbed from 6,262 to a record 9,075 on Jan 15, 2026, and the 10Y fell to 5.93% in October 2025 as foreign money returned and BI eased.

MSCI froze Indonesian index changes in January and on Oct 15 proposed Standalone status; BI hiked 100bp to 5.75% by June and now faces calls for more, while a wiretapping case against senior police officers adds political risk. JCI −46% to about 4,900, 10Y up 160bp to 7.72%: the second and deeper foreign exit.
notes.caveats: These are proxies, not reported fund flows: daily foreign SBN holdings (DJPPR) and equity flows (IDX) are not machine-readable for the dashboard, so the rupiah and the JCI stand in for foreign money. Before Oct 29, 2026 the 10Y is CNBC's benchmark-bond yield rather than PHEI's IGSYC, with repeated stale prints removed. The back-test runs from June 2022 (228 weeks): the live signal makes 91bp outright (Sharpe 0.37) against −73bp for always holding the 10Y; rally calls were right 49% of the time and sell-off calls 54%. Variants that use the US 10Y trend score higher over the whole sample (Sharpe up to 0.80) but were picked after the fact and are not live. Weekly data, 4-week horizon; not a trading system.
